comparison_arms: M01 and M02: condition record (bath Mg2+, K+, Ca2+ as measured values, temperature, perfusion rate, blockers actually present) and a time-matched vehicle arm, knockout, heterozygous and wild-type slices from littermates; every slice serves as its own baseline (within-slice paired design); a floor control for the delayed-response amplitude metric (wild-type reading at the same latency)
readouts: Measured bath composition; baseline burst incidence, frequency (own value, because the source gives 2.29 and 0.84 per minute for the same 119 bursts), duration with the unit stated; drift under vehicle
what_each_outcome_would_mean: A stable vehicle baseline makes later falls interpretable; drift or a bath that differs from the incubation ACSF changes how every arm is read; baseline frequency from this laboratory, not from either printed value, sets slice numbers
cost_note: Low; no drug; is a measurement need, not a literature question
existing_module_step_reused: X0 of nmda_inv05_20261107; P11 card magnesium gate step

comparison_arms: M07, M08 and M15: AMPA/kainate antagonist (perampanel; NBQX use-only) to a verified fast-EPSC block, d-APV added only if bursts persist; matched titrations of AMPA antagonist and d-APV on at least two metrics (evoked charge; peak current or fEPSP slope; recruited-cell fraction) together with a receptor-agnostic release-reducing control; genotype comparators
readouts: Fast fEPSP slope and mEPSC (verification), burst incidence, frequency, duration, burst-onset current, delayed response
what_each_outcome_would_mean: Bursts survive verified block: AMPA arm dropped for this preparation. Bursts abolished: not informative alone (loss of Mg2+ relief would abolish an NMDAR-regenerative burst too); informative only against the matched controls, and only if the ordering holds on both metrics and against the release-reducing control. Same curve as d-APV on both metrics: no receptor specificity
cost_note: Moderate; perampanel needs time to a steady block in slices (culture onset about 1 s at 3 uM, tissue unmeasured), and washout may not complete
existing_module_step_reused: Extends X3 (non-burst transmission spared?) of nmda_inv05; HYP-20261027-01 graded block

comparison_arms: M04, M05, M06 and M14: isolated NMDAR EPSC measured in the burst slices; d-APV titration; GluN2B NAM at matched percent removed; TCN-201 at two measured co-agonist levels with glycine alone; Mg2+ and K+ graded; terminal d-APV in every slice
readouts: Percent NMDAR EPSC removed, burst incidence and duration against it, delayed response, NAM-sensitive fraction, co-agonist level
what_each_outcome_would_mean: Left-shifted NAM curve: GluN2B-directed question; coincident curves: total gain; plateau with GluN2A-tool sensitivity at low but not high co-agonist: GluN2A question; effect that tracks Mg2+: state question
cost_note: High; isolated NMDAR EPSCs in P13-P17 neocortical pyramidal cells with blockers, many slices, slow-washout NAM allows one concentration per slice
existing_module_step_reused: X1 and X2 of nmda_inv05 (X1: isolated NMDAR current and NAM-sensitive fraction; X2: matched-current d-APV curve); X6 not applicable

comparison_arms: M09, M10, M11, M12 (held) and M13 (conditional): carbenoxolone with EPSCs, AP width, input resistance and a coupling readout; matched-effect control (graded antagonist and a receptor-agnostic release-reducing manipulation, two metrics); brilliant blue FCF with a validated Panx1 engagement readout; within-slice paired baselines
readouts: Burst frequency, duration; EPSC AMPA and NMDA; AP width; Rin; coupling coefficient or dye spread; engagement readout
what_each_outcome_would_mean: Matched control equals carbenoxolone: coupling not needed to explain the fall. Carbenoxolone stronger than matched control with coupling loss: connexin question stays open and motivates M13. Engagement shown and bursts fall: Panx1 supported
cost_note: Moderate to high; coupling readouts in layer II/III pyramidal pairs at P13-P17 are technically demanding; mefloquine and genetic routes need a prior reading or a cross
existing_module_step_reused: N-16 and the pannexin occlusion question named in NEED-EXCITATORY-GAIN-GLUTAMATE-RECEPTOR; no X step covers gap junctions

comparison_arms: Order of application inside each slice: baseline, drug to steady state, positive-control d-APV last for non-reversible agents (radiprodil, carbenoxolone, perampanel), washout only where the source shows reversal (d-APV)
readouts: Time stamps of each step; the same measured plateau criteria; each slice is its own baseline
what_each_outcome_would_mean: Prevents a non-reversing compound from being read as reversible or as run-down; allows an order effect to be tested by a second order in separate slices

comparison_arms: M16 (GABA-A disinhibition, separate slices from M04), M17 (kainate separation, open need: tool and its mechanism paper not read), M18 (pointer to hcn_20261107 for intrinsic excitability)
readouts: Burst frequency, duration; evoked IPSC; E/I ratio; for M17 kainate-evoked current as engagement
what_each_outcome_would_mean: GABA-A positive modulation abolishing bursts is compatible with alternative AB06 and equally with H4 (any large cut in drive); it is separated only by the evoked-IPSC and E/I measurements and does not by itself show that restored inhibition is sufficient or that NMDAR dependence is permissive; no change says the E/I reading is not the limiting step. Tovar's finding that carbenoxolone reduces IPSCs (fully reversible) could oppose a carbenoxolone burst fall, which is why M16 is kept
cost_note: Moderate for M16; M17 cannot be run until a kainate-selective tool and its primary mechanism reading exist (open need); M18 none here
existing_module_step_reused: No X step covers GABA-A or kainate; INV-18 package for the HCN question
